newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels say not asking for ransom money.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels say not asking for ransom money.

text.p: Marxist rebels holding 74 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima put a sign up to a window on Thursday denying government claims they were asking for ransom money from their captives.
"Do not lie Mr Fujimori. Money does not interest us. The demand is freedom of our prisoners," the sign said.
Over the last two days, President Alberto Fujimori's government has urged Japanese companies with representatives held captive not to give in to what he called the rebels' "blackmail".

Although the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) has in the past kidnapped businessmen and politicians to raise money, there has been no evidence that this was their aim in the current crisis. Their principal demand has been the release of about 400 jailed comrades.
In a second sign placed at the second-floor window, the rebels said they explained their position on Japanese hostages to two TV Asahi reporters who entered the residence on Tuesday.

"In the interview with Japan's TV Asahi, we explained the holding of Japanese diplomats and businessmen," the sign read. Police arrested the two reporters when they left the compound Tuesday and were still holding them, their notes and film of the interview.
